ledger.sentence: Ondansetron is an anti-sickness medicine used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy, radiotherapy and surgery.
ledger.note: Tablet leaflet lists the two licensed uses; MedlinePlus and GOSH agree

ledger.sentence: It belongs to the 5-HT3 receptor antagonist group, and the main cautions are an effect on the heart rhythm (QT prolongation) and use in early pregnancy.
ledger.note: NHS prescribing sheet: 5HT3 antagonist, dose-related QT prolongation; MHRA first-trimester warning (GOSH summary)

ledger.sentence: Preventing nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy or radiotherapy, with age limits that differ between the two uses.
Preventing nausea and vomiting after surgery.
Ondansetron is a specific 5-HT3 receptor antagonist, which blocks 5-HT3 receptors in the gut and in the central nervous system.
MedlinePlus says medicines in this group work by blocking serotonin, a natural substance that may cause nausea and vomiting.
Headache is very common with ondansetron, according to a UK leaflet.
ledger.note: Search summary of emc leaflet: headache very common

ledger.sentence: Constipation and flushing or a feeling of warmth are also listed as common.
ledger.note: Leaflet; GOSH lists warm flushes and headaches; NHS trust material adds constipation

ledger.sentence: Hiccups, low blood pressure and an irregular heartbeat are listed as uncommon effects.
A UK leaflet lists allergic reactions, chest pain and heart rhythm disturbances among the serious effects that call for medical help.
In an emergency the route to care is 999 or A&E; for an urgent concern that is not an emergency it is NHS 111 or a same-day GP appointment, and for routine questions a GP appointment or a pharmacist.
ledger.note: Site signposting rule: route to care named wherever urgency is mentioned

ledger.sentence: A UK leaflet says ondansetron must not be used with apomorphine (a Parkinson's disease medicine) or by anyone allergic to it.
The solution leaflet rules out use in the first three months of pregnancy.
ledger.note: Search summary of solution leaflet: first trimester

ledger.sentence: The MHRA has warned of a small increased risk of cleft lip or palate after first-trimester use, and says women should be counselled on benefits and risks before it is offered.
ledger.note: Search summary of GOSH page citing MHRA January 2020

ledger.sentence: An NHS Specialist Pharmacy Service page says ondansetron can be used with caution during breastfeeding, with monitoring of the baby.
Leaflets advise caution in people with a bowel blockage or severe constipation, heart failure, heart rhythm problems, liver problems or abnormal blood levels of potassium, sodium or magnesium.

An NHS prescribing sheet says ondansetron lengthens the QT interval (a measure of the heart's electrical cycle) in a dose-related way, and that torsade de pointes, a dangerous heart rhythm, has been reported, mainly with high intravenous doses.

The same sheet advises avoiding it in congenital long QT syndrome, and caution with heart failure, slow heart rates, other QT-prolonging medicines, and low potassium or magnesium, which are corrected before use.
The sheet also warns of serotonin syndrome when ondansetron is combined with medicines such as SSRIs, SNRIs and opioids.
An NHS prescribing sheet says low potassium and magnesium are corrected before use.
A prescriber considers heart rhythm risk when other QT-prolonging medicines are used.
ledger.note: NHS prescribing sheet: caution with other QT-prolonging drugs

ledger.sentence: Ondansetron is a prescription-only medicine in the UK; the emc listing for the 4 mg orodispersible tablets gives its legal status as POM.
A UK tablet leaflet lists two licensed uses for ondansetron: preventing nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy or radiotherapy, and preventing it after surgery.
MedlinePlus gives the same two groups of uses for adults taking the tablets.
Great Ormond Street Hospital describes it as a medicine that stops a child feeling sick and being sick.
It may be given by mouth as a tablet, melt or syrup, or as an injection into a vein.
Serotonin is a natural substance that can trigger nausea and vomiting.
ledger.note: MedlinePlus: a natural substance that may cause nausea and vomiting

ledger.sentence: Ondansetron blocks 5-HT3 receptors for serotonin in the gut and in the central nervous system.
Medicines in this group are called 5-HT3 receptor antagonists.
Great Ormond Street Hospital notes that some medicines can react with ondansetron and change how well it works, so a doctor or pharmacist is asked about other medicines first.
